<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **46** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**39** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 43 pages)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1004696bc3bb3fb8c743aac7fb77603d07e2de6e` — the merge of head `41ae3536caaa9c7afb51033837143364d92be433` into base `45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1004696bc3bb3fb8c743aac7fb77603d07e2de6e && git checkout 1004696bc3bb3fb8c743aac7fb77603d07e2de6e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16 41ae3536caaa9c7afb51033837143364d92be433 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16 && git merge --no-ff 41ae3536caaa9c7afb51033837143364d92be433

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45f0f81fb0cab0f51de2f89117cfd642d4020a16` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `988fc23b8fc88b53faefebc86057b8a442bfbd9f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/mapping.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sourced-mapping-upserts-into-synced-object.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sync-field-prefix-reserved.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts, packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts, ui/packages/types/src/managed-by.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/components/ManagedByBadge.tsx

Inputs read: card #32061 (body, 4 comments, the os-dev-report included), PR #32118 (body, 44 files, net diff against merge-base `ff04ad81`), the check-runs on the head, and `docs/adr/0153-one-way-sync-in-beside-federation.md` on `main` (D1 to D4, D8, the P2 spec row), with ADR-0049 and ADR-0103 (D1 and the 2026-07-20 addendum) to judge it. `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` has no source change in the diff (tests only); it was read, not reviewed.

Check-runs on the head at the time of this record: 23 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, 32 still in progress. Concluded green and relevant here: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, the three scoped lints, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate. **Pending, not judged here:** Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI. This verdict is the design judgment on what has concluded; the pending runs remain the gate verdicts, and a red one among them is not covered by this PASS. Type Check UI is the only measurement of the `ManagedByBadge.tsx` edit (the dev reported it NOT MEASURED locally).

### ① Derived judgments

- **`data.Mapping` accept set, widened: right.** `datasourceSource` (`object`, `watermark.field`, `watermark.start`, `full`, `deletePolicy`, `deletedField`), and on `connectorSource` the keys `paging` (`style` of page, cursor, offset, none; `param`; `nextPath`), `deletePolicy`, `deletedField`. Shapes match D1 to D3. `deletePolicy` declares no `.default()` and the parse adds no key (pinned in `mapping-sync-in.test.ts`), as D3 requires for its liveness row. All four land as `planned` rows with `authorWarn` on `packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json`; Spec property liveness is green.
- **`data.Mapping` accept set, narrowed at parse: right.** Both sources together; a sourced mapping whose `mode` is not `upsert` (the default `insert` included); a sourced upsert with no or an empty `upsertKey`; `paging` whose style lacks its `param`, a cursor with no `nextPath`, and `none` beside either. D1, D2 and D4 each state these. An unsourced mapping is untouched (`sources.length === 0` returns first), so the import door keeps its accept set.
- **`defineStack` accept set, narrowed: right.** Sourced target not `managedBy: 'synced'` (either source); `datasourceSource.object` not an object of the stack, or carrying no `external` binding; `source_key_missing`; `source_key_not_exact`; a non-halvable `watermark.field`; `watermark_not_exact`; `watermark_field_unmapped`. Each is in the ADR row. All ride the registered `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` / 422 envelope.
- **`job.pull`, widened: right.** `collectJobPullMappingErrors` accepts either source (D1).
- **`data.Object` accept set: right.** `managedBy` gains `synced` (widening); `userActions` opening create, import, edit or delete on a `synced` object is refused at parse (narrowing, the named exception to ADR-0103 D1); a field key starting `_sync_` is refused in `ObjectSchema.fields` and `ObjectExtensionSchema.fields` (narrowing; `fieldPatches` keeps the plain grammar, correctly, since it declares no field). The reservation is a second `.regex()`, so the published JSON Schema states it.
- **Public surface: right.** New export `MANAGED_BY_WRITE_LOCKED_BUCKETS` from `@objectstack/spec/data` (one row in `api-surface/data.json`), read by `@objectstack/core`. `resolveCrudAffordances` changes behaviour only for the new bucket. `ENGINE_OWNED_BUCKETS` (exported from plugin-security) gains a member. `ManagedByBucket` and `MANAGED_BY_BUCKETS` in `@object-ui/types` gain a member, which is a compile-time narrowing for any exhaustive consumer; the one in this repo is handled (see ④).
- **Dropped refinements: right and declared.** The `MappingSchema` and `paging` refinements have no JSON Schema projection; `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` records the sites.
- **ADR-0087: right.** Two semantic entries, each a structured TODO rather than a conversion, with the reason stated (the key column and the new field name are author intent). The changeset carries the registration marker for both ids.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the PR body and the changeset match the card, the ADR row and the diff (widening keys beside narrowing refusals; the strongest kind named). One changeset, `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `lint`, `objectql`, `core`, `plugin-security` and `@object-ui/types`, marked BREAKING with a before and after block and both migration ids: these are exactly the packages whose `src` changes outside tests. `organizations` and `cloud-connection` change tests only and are correctly unbumped; `@object-ui/app-shell` is private. Check Changeset concluded success. Level agrees with what the diff publishes.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Private synced object with no read sharing rule: warning not implemented. Accepted for this card; ESCALATED for a carrier, and the dev's recommendation A is not adopted.** The P2 spec row names only the `security-owd-unset` fix-it from that paragraph of D4, and the fix-it is delivered and already tells the author that `private` needs a sharing rule that grants read. But D4 does decide the warning ("is warned at author time"), and no row of the children table places it. It is a lint rule in `packages/lint`; the P3 Studio child is `ui` and the P3 guide child is skills, and neither owns that package. Option B is the right one: a separate lint card, filed through triage under the epic #31763, before the P2 engine card lets a pull fill a `private` synced object. Until a card exists this is an ADR decision with no owner, so the seat should send the `Request: triage`, not leave it as an acceptance note.
2. **`watermark_field_unmapped` judged at build for `datasourceSource` only: accepted (A).** D3 is explicit: the build refusal is the datasource source's ("A datasource source must copy its watermark into the target ... or the mapping is refused at build"), and "the connector source already needs that copy, because its starting point is read from the target today", which is the executor's own run-time reason. A connector watermark is a response path the stack cannot type. The implementation matches the ADR sentence for sentence.
3. **No ADR-0112 codes for the finding names: accepted (A).** The registered code is the envelope's (`STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID`), as for every other cross-reference finding; the ADR asks for refusal "by name", and each name is a stable token in the finding, pinned by a test. One consequence to carry to #32062: D2 invariant 7 has the run refuse "with the same reason", so the engine card must reuse these exact tokens (`source_key_not_exact`, `watermark_not_exact`).

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`, each checked against the tree:
- runtime `judgeJobPull` still refuses a mapping with no `connectorSource` (`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts:509`): true, carrier #32062 is right. Note for that card: the install-local refusal sentence (`packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1111`) tells the author to add a `connectorSource` and says "`os validate` refuses the same `pull`"; for a `datasourceSource` pull both halves are now false until the engine card lands.
- `ManagedByBadge` draws nothing for `synced`: true and safe (④). Carrier P3 Studio is right.
- ADR-0153 status line still reads Proposed: true on `main`; `docs/adr/` is outside the claim, and the seat carries it.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix and no should-fix. Six nits, none fixed on this head (each is outside the prose faces, so a fix would move the head): each is an accepted deviation with the follow-up named.

**`hits` files**

- `packages/spec/src/data/mapping.zod.ts`: holds against D1 to D4. The exclusive-source refusal, the mode and key refusal (`:669` onward) and the `paging` refinement are the ADR's sentences; the `deleteMode` guidance now lands on `deletePolicy` while `conflictResolution` and `direction` keep the no-policy sentence, which is still true. The jsdoc that says the block is "READ BY NOTHING YET" agrees with the ledger. Tried: both sources, default mode, empty key, `none` with a param, a `deletePolicy` outside the enum. All refused; legal twins silent.
- `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`: holds. The affordance row equals `engine-owned`'s; `resolveCrudAffordances` drops every write override on the locked bucket and keeps `exportCsv`, so an unparsed document that opens a verb still resolves closed (defence beside the parse refusal); the parse refusal treats `true` and the object form with `enabled: true` as opening, which is exactly what `normalizeRowCrudOverride` treats as opening (an object form with no `enabled` falls back to the closed base). `MANAGED_BY_WRITE_LOCKED_BUCKETS` is declared below its first reader but is only read at parse time, so there is no ordering hazard. `ObjectExtensionSchema` declares neither `managedBy` nor `userActions`, so an extension cannot reopen the bucket. `resolveInjectedSystemColumns` already withholds `owner_id` from any object with `managedBy` set and keeps the tenant column, which is D4's "no person owner" and D8's organization with no edit.
- `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`: holds against the ADR row, with the nits below. `columnMap` is read remote to local, which is the binding's declared direction; the integer bound of 15 digits is inside 2^53 and `precision` is total digits at `scale: 0`; the watermark copy check reads the parsed mapping, where `transform` is defaulted to `none`. An `external` binding on a datasource this stack declares managed is refused by the existing `collectExternalBindingDatasourceErrors`, so "federated" is not satisfied by a block alone.
  - **nit · `stack.zod.ts:4826` and `:4902`.** `source_key_not_exact` is judged only when the source object declares an `id` field. A federated object that maps a remote `BIGINT` onto `id` and declares no `id` field passes the build (the test's own legal twin declares none). This is inside the ADR's letter ("refused at build, from the declared type", and "a declaration can be wrong" with a run-time refusal), but it makes the build refusal avoidable by omission. Follow-up on #32062: the run-time refusal of a numeric key outside the safe range must cover an undeclared `id` too.
  - **nit · `stack.zod.ts:5604` against `:5700` and the comment at `:4836`.** `collectSourcedMappingErrors` runs after the `objectNames.size === 0` early return, so a stack that declares a sourced mapping and no object is judged for nothing: not the synced target, not the source object. The comment "a target this stack does not define is already refused there" is false for that stack, because the target check sits behind the same return. The gap is the existing `targetObject` rule's own, inherited; the build cannot see a sibling package's objects. Follow-up on #32062: the pull judges the target's bucket where the object is known.
  - **nit · `stack.zod.ts:4883` to `:4888`.** An object on an external datasource that declares no `external` block is federated by ADR-0015 (the block only describes the binding), yet it is told its rows "are already local and there is nothing to copy". The refusal itself is right, since without `columnMap` there is no key; the sentence is wrong for that author, and `source_key_missing` is the honest finding.
  - **nit, for the seat to carry · `stack.zod.ts:4860` to `:4866`.** Nothing refuses a sourced target that itself carries an `external` binding, nor `datasourceSource.object` naming the mapping's own `targetObject`. An object that is both `synced` and federated passes every check here, and a pull would then write a remote table as the system. ADR-0153 lists no such refusal, so this is not a deviation from the contract; it is a hole in the ADR's list that #32062 or a dated ADR note should close before a reader exists.
  - **nit, for the seat to carry.** `upsertKey` is required but not tied to the mapping: a key naming a target field that no `fieldMapping` entry writes parses and builds, and an upsert on it matches nothing, which is the duplicate-every-run loss D4 refused `insert` for. Not in the ADR row; a candidate for the engine card's refusals.
- `packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts`: holds. The jsdoc sentence "the binder does not schedule it" (`:386`) is true on this head: `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` logs and skips a pull that `judgeJobPull` does not bind. The published describe changed only to name either source.
- `18.sourced-mapping-upserts-into-synced-object.ts`: holds. Surface, replacement and acceptance criteria state the three parse rules, the target rule and the `userActions` rule, each as the diff enforces it. No conversion is claimed, and none is possible.
- `18.sync-field-prefix-reserved.ts`: holds. It names both field records, excludes `fieldPatches`, and says the stored column moves with the rename. One hazard to hand to #32062, not a defect here: the reservation lives in the key grammar of `ObjectSchema.fields`, so the engine card's injected `_sync_` columns must never be re-parsed through `ObjectSchema` after injection.

**Implementing files**

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts`: agrees. `synced` joins `ENGINE_OWNED_BUCKETS`; the affordance check reads the locked resolver, so no `userActions` passes a member write; system and context-less writes bypass, which is how D8's pull writes. The bucket's own 403 sentence is accurate.
- `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (read, not in the diff): the reconciliation covers `synced` with no edit, because `checkManagedApiMethodAffordances` judges every object with `managedBy` set through `resolveCrudAffordances`; the new test pins that every write verb is stripped even when `userActions` opens them.
  - **nit, follow-up card · `registry.ts:1996` and `packages/spec/src/data/managed-api-affordance.ts:149`** (both outside the diff). For a `synced` object the strip warning and the lint sentence tell the author to "Declare userActions to open a verb" and "needs userActions edit", a declaration the parse now refuses. The message is wrong for this one bucket; the strip is right.
- `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts`: agrees. `synced` joins `GUARDED_WRITE_BUCKETS`, and the clamp reads an empty `userActions` on a locked bucket, so `allowCreate`, `allowEdit`, `allowDelete`, `allowTransfer` and `modifyAllRecords` all come down, matching what the guard refuses.
- `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts` and `packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts`: agree. Both mirrors take `synced`, their prose tables are updated to seven and four buckets, and each is pinned against the spec enum by its test.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`: agrees with D4. The fix-it recommends `public_read` and names the sharing rule `private` needs; a synced object skips the external-ownership arm, correctly, since it is a local copy. `isSystemObject` does not exempt it, so the rule still fires.
- `ui/packages/types/src/managed-by.ts`: agrees. Union and list both gain the member, in the enum's order.
- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/components/ManagedByBadge.tsx` (outside the claimed surface): the one-line exclusion is safe. `variantOf` reads `VARIANTS[...] ?? null` (`:191`), so `synced` draws no badge and cannot throw; the claim in the comment that the buttons are already closed is true, because `@object-ui/core`'s `resolveEffectiveCrudAffordances` delegates to the spec resolver. Drawing no badge is the honest choice over borrowing `engine-owned`'s copy. It weakens the "a new bucket is a compile error to miss" property for this one member until the P3 Studio child removes the exclusion; that child should carry it by name. Whether it compiles is Type Check UI's verdict, which is pending.

**ADR-0049 judgment.** The bucket does not land unenforced: the enum value arrives in the same diff as the guard set, the resolver lock that the reconciliation reads, the clamp, both mirrors and the UI union, each with a pinned test, and the two ablations on the PR body show the guard and the target refusal are load-bearing. The readers the ADR says keep their answer (`user-assigned-work`, both seed-ownership passes, the install-local seed owner, `outlivesOrganization`) were read on the head: each tests `managedBy` for presence or for two named buckets, so each skips or excludes `synced` as D4 states, with no edit needed.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-dsw4lt`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzh7cM8EmUX4T2CBNHX` (isolated contract-review sub-agent of the seat's session; did not write the diff)

**VERDICT: PASS**

domain:spec#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzh7cM8EmUX4T2CBNHX

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：同步导入的 spec 半边落地。
  - `mapping` 新增 `datasourceSource`（与 `connectorSource` 二选一）、`paging`、`deletePolicy`、`deletedField`，都标 `planned` 并提醒作者。
  - 构建期新增一组拒绝：带来源的 mapping 必须 upsert 进 `managedBy: 'synced'` 对象，源键和水位要精确、可映射，不接受联邦源对象。
  - 新安全分桶 `synced` 连同全部执行机制一起上线：写入守卫、apiMethods 收敛、`/me/permissions` 收紧、两处镜像、UI 桶联合。
  - 所有对象保留 `_sync_` 字段前缀。
- 为什么改：ADR-0153（epic #31763），要让外部数据（含数仓表）成为只读的普通对象，再交给后续的 engine 卡（#32062）实现读取。
- 风险与回滚：属于收紧（破坏性），已登记 ADR-0087 迁移两条。实测仓内与 hotcrm 都没有受影响的写法。CLI 集成测试里有三个夹具按新规则改正了，断言没动。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` 的 `collectSourcedMappingErrors`，`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` 的 `synced` 行，以及 `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/mapping-sync-in.test.ts src/data/object-managed-by-synced.test.ts`，预期全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

席位意见：fable 契约复审 PASS（6762969887），没有必改和建议改，6 条 nit 都作为已接受偏差处理，各有去处。之后新 head 上 CI 暴露了 4 处本 PR 引起的测试红：1 处 UI 桶数钉子，3 处 CLI 夹具。卡线程已全部修好，同时把整树里 `connectorSource` 的用法清查了一遍，改动只涉及测试、夹具和两页文档，源码没动，所以不需要增量复审。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · domain:spec#3 · head `41ae3536caaa9c7afb51033837143364d92be433`

- **Shape:** 52 files (+1582 −87) on merge base `ff04ad81`. The source is the contract-reviewed set at `988fc23b`:
  - `mapping.zod.ts`: four keys and the parse refusals;
  - `stack.zod.ts`: the build cross-reference refusals and `job.pull` accepting either source;
  - `object.zod.ts`: the `synced` enum value, its affordance row, the `userActions` exception and the `_sync_` reservation;
  - the enforcement set: guard, clamp, both mirrors, `ui` union, and the `security-owd-unset` fix-it;
  - two semantic migration entries, the liveness rows, and the regenerated baselines.

  `988fc23b..41ae3536` adds tests, fixtures and two docs pages only (8 files, +27 −9). No source file moved.
- **Premise measured:** at `48f18b58` there was no `datasourceSource` anywhere, `managedBy` had six values, and the enforcement set held `engine-owned` / `append-only` only (claim 6760447505).
